intro: Buddhists do not only read their scriptures. They live them. They keep festivals through the year. They meet in temples to chant, listen and share food. In this unit, you will visit Buddhist festivals and communities, from Asia to Chicago.
First you will learn about Vesak, Hanamatsuri, Uposatha, Kathina, Obon and Losar. Then you will learn how Buddhist temples began in Chicago and what you might see if you visit one.
By the end, you will be able to name the main Buddhist festivals and tell what each remembers. You will be able to describe a temple visit and explain how to be a respectful guest.
bigQuestion: How do Buddhist festivals and temples help people remember the Buddha and care for each other?

write.prompt: Pick two Buddhist festivals from this unit. What does each one help Buddhists remember? Use one story or text from the unit, like the Vinaya's rains rule or the Ullambana Sutra, and tell how Buddhists keep the day.
tips: Name the festival and the country or tradition that keeps it.
Say 'Buddhists believe' or 'the story tells' when you tell a belief.
Name the text you use, like the Vinaya or the Ullambana Sutra.
Use unit words like sangha, merit and offerings.
